title: Anthropic's IPO: Safety vs. Scrutiny
caption:
Anthropic's rumored IPO means massive capital but also intense scrutiny. Can a company built on ethical AI principles truly thrive under Wall Street's relentless pursuit of quarterly growth? It's a high-stakes gamble for the Claude maker.

Flowi cuts through the market hype, giving you the real story on AI's biggest moves.

slides.headline: IPO isn't the *only* way to win the AI race. Anthropic's bet is a big one.
slides.sub: The Claude maker considers going public.

slides.title: WHY GO PUBLIC NOW?
slides.body: Accessing massive capital for R&D and compute is paramount. Competing with OpenAI and Google demands resources. An IPO provides liquidity for early investors and employees, attracting top talent in a tight market.

slides.title: CAPITAL & VISIBILITY
bullets: Billions in new funding to scale models and infrastructure.
Increased brand awareness and market legitimacy.
Liquidity for early investors and employee stock options.
Positions Anthropic as a long-term AI leader.

slides.title: SCRUTINY & PRESSURE
bullets: Intense regulatory oversight on AI safety and ethics claims.
Public market volatility impacts valuation and investor confidence.
Pressure to prioritize quarterly profits over long-term research.
Increased competition from open-source models and tech giants.

audiences.body: Built on a "constitutional AI" safety framework. Prioritizes responsible development. Aims for beneficial AI, not just powerful AI.
Focuses on revenue growth, market share, and profitability. Short-term returns often outweigh long-term ethical considerations.

slides.sub: Learn to build with AI, no investor deck needed.
